claim: Two parts of ADV-4's narrowed set-aside range are not pinned by any self-test, although the disposition says 'V97 pins it'. The first is the platform-check part: with the platform's arrival check, only pings at or after the indication count. The second is the part of CW-R06's moment range after the indication (up to TS_TOLERANCE_S). V97's outlier sits 135 s after the mark, outside both parts. Each mutation flips the tier of a no-show uphold and still passes the whole suite.
how: V96 rebuilt so the outlier is the last ping in the moment range (R11); V96B (pings at the pin after it, R8 AUTO), V100 (platform check, outlier before the indication, R8 AUTO) and V101 (platform check, outlier after the indication that would contradict it, R11) pin both parts.

claim: A3-FID-01's fix is observable but not pinned. The fix attributes F-PRESENCE to CW-F04B so that decisive lists stop naming CW-R06 or CW-F06. Reverting it passes every test, and the disposition's evidence 'V04F and V48 now report CW-F04B, not CW-R06' is not asserted: neither variant has a 'decisive' expectation, and the decisive check is containment, so an extra CW-R06 would not fail.
how: V04F expects CW-F04B decisive and CW-R06 and CW-F06 not decisive (new not_decisive expectation in the self-test).

claim: ADV-4's narrowed definition was not carried everywhere. D29's own implementation note still opens with the pre-ADV-4 range, which contradicts its later sentence and CW-F04B. The CW-R06 census row note has the same stale range. Both contradict the engine and V97.
how: D29 note and the CW-R06 census row state the narrowed range.

claim: SG-2's correction was applied to CW-R06 and its census row but not to D39 (a). D39 (a) still records Jasper's judgment on the false premise that every row resting on CW-R06's FairRyde parts is D.
how: D39 (a) states the R6 exception (CW-F03B start test).

claim: SG-6 split FC-F03's rider-agreement element in the census: agreement before the trip is B, a request during the trip is FAIRRYDE (D). The FC-F03 rule card was not updated. Its credibility_note still counts three FairRyde elements and calls rider agreement Ryde text, and no FAIRRYDE source note labels the mid-trip request. CLAUDE.md requires every rule element to have a source or an open FairRyde label.
how: FC-F03 credibility_note counts four FairRyde elements, rider agreement before the trip is B, and the FAIRRYDE source labels the request during the trip.

claim: The engine's D29 parameter trigger is broader than the rule text. CW-F04B and AUTH-02 trigger 12 limit it to CW-F04B's five parameters, but the engine fires it for any C or D parameter whose end makes F-GPS-LOGIC true, and labels it '(CW-F04B, D29)'. The tier is unchanged for no-show fees, because clause 2 already makes the moving parameter decisive.
how: The engine's parameter trigger covers CW-F04B's parameters only.

claim: CW-F04B's F-GPS-LOGIC text names the set-aside kind by flag ('was set aside (GPS_OUTLIER or GPS_DATA_ERROR)'). But when the set-aside ping lies in CW-R06's moment range outside the window, the engine makes F-GPS-LOGIC true and raises no GPS_OUTLIER flag, because the flag is raised only for outlier runs that touch the window.
how: CW-F04B says "set aside as an outlier or a data error" without naming the flags, which are raised only for pings touching the window.

claim: The radius-cost table (600 clean upholds, AUTO 235 to 29) comes from a script in the builder's scratch that is not in the repo, so that part of the tier report cannot be rerun from its inputs. Every other number in the report reproduces. An independent simulation corroborates the magnitude.
how: The simulation is in the repo (validation/build_checks/A3/jitter_sim.py) and the tier report names the command; the census generator is there too (make_census.py).

claim: Frozen area (D34): the defect that ADV-3 fixed for GPS pings (ordering by timestamp text instead of by instant) remains in the rider-message reading. answers_question sorts the driver's messages by their timestamp string. A3 did not change this code; it is the same class of pre-existing defect.
how: Frozen area (D34): D39 (k), not fixed.

claim: CW-F04's credibility_note and the census row for its window element justify B by quoting the main policy page as "waits ... at the pick-up point". In the source, 'at the pick-up point' belongs to 'for the rider to arrive', so the clause does not say where the driver waits. The window end ('leaving after the threshold does not count') is recorded in open item D26 as a team decision, and the census does not cite D26. The B label can still stand on RYDE-4407754403353 and FX4's own core ('driver at the pick-up per GPS while waiting, B'), but the stated basis is a misreading. The element is the one on which an automatic uphold like V34 rests.
how: CW-F04 cites the article's joined conditions ('Has waited for more than 3 mins') and its note no longer misquotes the main policy page; census row updated.

claim: Round 1's SG-6 fix split the FC-F03 census row: a route agreed before the trip is B, and a request or agreement during the trip (including avoiding ERP at the rider's request) is FAIRRYDE, D. The FC-F03 card was not updated. Its FAIRRYDE source covers only the navigation-record rule. Its credibility_note calls rider agreement 'Ryde text ... so B' and lists only three D elements, so the during-trip element has no FairRyde label on the card.
how: Same as FID2-05.

claim: After the ADV-4 fix, CW-F04B and the engine count a set-aside ping only if it could change the presence (in the window) or the arrival (CW-R06's moment range; with the platform check, only at or after the indication). Two texts still state the old range, from PING_MAX_GAP_S before the arrival to the window end: census row 27, which justifies CW-R06's 'delegated' outlier element, and the first parenthetical of D29's decide note. The DT-CW-NOSHOW note and the ontology label still summarize the finding as 'a ping set aside' without the qualifier. ADV-4's disposition says the census agrees with the engine, but this row was not updated.
how: Same as FID2-03; CW-F04B census rows reworded.

claim: CW-F04B's English and zh say no waiver rests on its logic. Yet F-GPS-LOGIC includes the later confirmation (ARRIVAL_UNCONFIRMED), and a short-wait waiver (R6) can rest on the wait start it moves. CW-R06 and the DT-CW-NOSHOW note say exactly this since round 1's SG-2 fix. SG-2 corrected the same overstatement in CW-R06 but not in CW-F04B.
how: CW-F04B (English and zh): the waiver statement covers LEFT and FALSE only; a short-wait waiver on a later confirmation is covered by CW-F03B's start test.

claim: CW-R06's round 1 sentence (English and zh) and its credibility_note list R3 among the rows on which 'an upheld fee or an escalation' rests. R3 is a waiver (WAIVE_FEE), not an upheld fee or an escalation.
how: CW-R06 statement, zh and note: R2 escalation, R3 waiver that needs approval, R9 and R11 upheld fees.

claim: F-GPS-LOGIC (CW-F04B) misses the window-edge logic D29 names ('window edges'). The rules treat the driver as present across an unobserved change of position at a window edge. One case: the last ping at the pin is more than TS_TOLERANCE_S before the window end and the next ping is outside, more than TS_TOLERANCE_S after the window end. The other: a real departure before the window start, with the driver first seen back more than TS_TOLERANCE_S into the window. In both, F-GPS-LOGIC is false at the base values and at every parameter end, so the fee is upheld at AUTO. A shorter or earlier-detected version of the same pattern goes to approval through GPS_AMBIGUOUS. The presence logic predates A3 (the de53c7c engine gives the same AUTO), but A3's F-GPS-LOGIC was meant to cover it. The same hole reaches waiting fees through the rule text.
how: GPS_AMBIGUOUS covers both window edges (engine, CW-F04B English and zh, taxonomy label): a stretch first seen away before the cancellation (or within the tolerance of the window end) after a last inside ping more than TS_TOLERANCE_S before the window end, and a window that starts after the arrival while the driver was last seen away and is not back within TS_TOLERANCE_S. V102 and V103 pin it; the fuzz invariant checks the end edge; explain.py states the reason with times and IDs.

claim: After the sort-by-instant fix (ADV-3), pings written in another UTC offset are decided correctly. Their times are still displayed in the ping's own offset, so the trace and the explanation mix clock times. The wait start taken from a ping (CW-F03B) is printed in UTC next to local times.
how: Pings are read on the trip record's clock (astimezone), so traces and explanations no longer mix offsets.

claim: A GPS timestamp with no UTC offset makes E.run raise TypeError, so the case gets no ruling and no tier, instead of a flag such as RECORDS_MISSING with approval. With some pings naive, the new sort itself fails. With all of them naive, the comparison with the arrival fails. This is not an unsafe AUTO, and the crash predates A3 in effect.
how: Pre-existing: D39 (j); a timestamp without an offset stops the engine (no ruling, no tier); normalizing it needs a data-quality rule.

claim: The D29 parameter trigger fires on any C or D parameter at whose plausible-range end F-GPS-LOGIC becomes true, not only on CW-F04B's five parameters. It then tells the reviewer that 'FairRyde's own GPS logic' would decide with a non-GPS parameter. AUTH-02 trigger 12 limits the trigger to CW-F04B's parameters. The tier is unaffected because clause 2 already makes the row move decisive.
how: Same as FID2-06.

claim: PB-CW-WAITING step 5 says 'Presence and F-GPS-LOGIC as for a no-show fee, over the free wait'. An LLM applier can read 'over the free wait' as the scope of F-GPS-LOGIC. CW-F04B's F-GPS-LOGIC also counts set-aside pings in CW-R06's arrival range before the window, and a later confirmation. Read that way, a waiting fee whose arrival rests on a set-aside ping before the free wait comes out AUTO.
how: Skeptic refuted it.

claim: The round 1 fix (ADV-4) means to count a set-aside ping only if it 'could change' the arrival. The text, and the engine with it, instead counts every set-aside ping anywhere in CW-R06's moment range. But CW-R06 reads only the last remaining ping in that range, so an outlier earlier than a remaining ping in the range cannot change the arrival. V96, the variant added to pin this rule, is such a case. Its R11 explanation tells both parties something false: that the arrival and stay rest on FairRyde's reading of a point that could not have changed anything.
how: A set-aside ping in the moment range counts only if it would otherwise have been CW-R06's moment ping (no remaining ping after it in the range); engine, CW-F04B (English and zh), ontology label, DT note, D29 and the census agree; V96, V96B, V100, V101.

claim: The round 1 fix narrowed which set-aside pings count (ADV-4), but the old range still stands in D29's first definition and in the census row for CW-R06's outlier element, and they contradict CW-F04B. The ontology label for F-GPS-LOGIC and the DT-CW-NOSHOW credibility note still say just 'a ping set aside', with no range.
how: Same as CONS2-1 for the ontology label and the DT note; D29 and the census row as in FID2-03.

claim: A3 added an after-window sentence that tells the parties the point after the counted wait 'is not counted as leaving'. In V54 that point is exactly what makes the departure unsettled (GPS_AMBIGUOUS, the reason the case needs approval). The explanation never says why it is unsettled, and the new sentence reads as if the driver was certainly present for the whole counted wait. The missing reason is older than A3: line 192 skips the 'gap' kind as 'already stated', but the set-aside sentence covers only outliers inside the window.
how: explain.py states why the pings cannot settle the question (gap, end and start kinds, with times and IDs) and drops the "not counted as leaving" sentence for a point that makes the departure unsettled (V54, V96, V102, V103).

claim: Several A3 open-item records misstate the rules or the review evidence: D39 (g) and (a), D39's list of added sources, and D31.
